Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters OpenAI OpenAI ‘ethically hacked’ with help of Anthropic’s Claude chatbot US cybersecurity researchers who conducted hack say ‘scope of what we could theoretically access was huge’ Dan Milmo Global technology editor Fri 18 Sep 2026 07.20 EDT Last modified on Fri 18 Sep 2026 10.49 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Cybersecurity researchers have hacked into OpenAI with the help of Anthropic’s Claude chatbot, in the latest example of security issues at the company. A team at a US-based startup compromised a number of OpenAI employees’ ChatGPT accounts, starting a process that enabled them to access their target’s software cache – and potentially more. “The scope of what we could theoretically access was huge,” said researchers at Hacktron AI . Initially, the research team used Claude, which can generate code for hackers, to access ChatGPT accounts via an OpenAI staff discussion forum hosted by the Discourse platform. They then made a harmless “pull request” – an attempt to change the code in a file – to OpenAI’s service on the GitHub software repository. Hacktron reported the hack to OpenAI, having carried out the operation under an OpenAI programme that rewarded ethical hackers for testing its systems. The researchers stressed that they had access to, but did not download, the code from the GitHub repository. Despite initial use of Claude, the researchers said they were largely using OpenAI’s own cutting edge GPT-5.6 Sol model to carry out the hack, which was first reported by the Wall Street Journal. An OpenAI spokesperson said: “We thank the researchers for contacting us and sharing their findings”, adding that the company had addressed the vulnerabilities that had been exploited. Hacktron said AI tools had made a once-complex hacking task far easier and drastically shortened the time needed to plan and execute an attack. This is a common refrain from cybersecurity experts when discussing the impact of AI. “Work that once required a well-resourced team and months of effort can now be compressed into days,” said Hacktron, which received a $6,500 payment from OpenAI under the company’s bug bounty programme. The hack is the latest safety incident at OpenAI, which revealed in July that a “swarm” of agents – the term for AI tools capable of carrying out tasks autonomously – powered by its technology had hacked the AI startup Hugging Face during a cybersecurity test. This week the San Francisco-based company revealed six more examples of “unexpected or concerning” actions by its technology, and warned that the pace of development could not continue at “maximum speed for much longer”. Anthropic made a fresh call at the weekend for a slowdown in AI development , which was supported by OpenAI, Google DeepMind and Elon Musk. Anthropic also repeated warnings that unrestrained AI development posed an existential threat, concerns that some experts are sceptical about. Donald Trump has rejected calls for a slowdown, citing a need to stay ahead of China’s AI industry and dismissing “negative forces … bringing up things that won’t happen”. https://www.dw.com/en/nuremberg-airport-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OCUe Special police units at Nuremberg airport after an alert aboard a passenger plane prompted a temporary closure Image: Tizian Gerbing/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Police gave the all-clear at Germany's Nuremberg airport after a suspected in-flight emergency involving a plane arriving from the Greek island of Corfu. The alert prompted police to cordon off the airport and Eurofighter jets to escort the aircraft, which landed safely, an airport spokesman said. Authorities confirmed later on Tuesday that the airport had resumed normal operations. Coredon Airlines, which was operating the flight in question, said they believed an emergency signal had been sent due to a technical malfunction. Why was the airport closed? The DPA news agency reported that the plane had transmitted an emergency code before landing, alerting air traffic control to a possible problem on board. "Checks at the scene established that there is no danger," police said in a statement. The nature of the alert was not immediately clear. Earlier in the morning, three pilots independently reported seeing an object that may have been a drone while taking off or landing at the airport. An onboard alert on a Corendon flight from Corfu prompted a temporary closure of Nuremberg airport Image: Daniel Löb/dpa/picture alliance Airport officials, border police and Germany's air traffic control service immediately launched a search involving a police helicopter, but no drone was found. Six flights were delayed, while two arriving aircraft diverted to Cologne and Prague before continuing to Nuremberg. It was initially unclear whether the two incidents were connected. Drone incidents disrupt German airports German airports have faced drone-related security alerts previously. In August, an explosives-laden drone was found near a runway at Leipzig/Halle airport , prompting a police investigation. Leipzig drone threat prompts security concerns in Germany To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video In May, a possible drone sighting halted flights at Munich airport for about an hour, forcing more than 20 arriving aircraft to divert. Police found no drone. Photograph: PR IMAGE View image in fullscreen Brendan Nugent has been named as the man arrested over the alleged vehicle attack on Indi MP Helen Haines in Wangaratta on Monday. Photograph: PR IMAGE Helen Haines Brendan Nugent’s family say Helen Haines has been their friend for more than 20 years Father of 43-year-old Tarrawingee man who allegedly attacked the independent MP says incident is ‘devastating and unfathomable’ Who is Helen Haines, the MP allegedly attacked in Victoria? Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Henry Belot and Nino Bucci Tue 20 Oct 2026 06.37 EDT First published on Mon 19 Oct 2026 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The father of a 43-year-old man accused of allegedly attacking Helen Haines has pledged to work with police and described the incident as “shocking and horrific”. The independent MP remained in a critical condition on Tuesday after being airlifted from Wangaratta in northern Victoria to Melbourne’s Alfred hospital for emergency surgery on Monday night. She has lost one leg, with surgeons working to save the other. Police confirmed a 43-year-old Tarrawingee man alleged to have driven the Toyota LandCruiser was arrested at the scene. Brendan Nugent was charged on Tuesday night with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the Commonwealth offence of causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Victoria police confirmed in a statement that they would allege the attack was targeted. Nugent is expected to appear at Wangaratta magistrates court on Wednesday. ‘I don’t want to be known as a hero’: barber who rushed to help Helen Haines praised by PM Read more In a statement, Brendan Nugent’s father, Rod Nugent, and Rod’s partner, Christine Cunningham, said Haines had been their friend for more than 20 years. “What happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable,” they said. “We would like to sincerely thank members of the local community and police who came to Helen’s aid yesterday … We will be assisting Victoria Police in any way we can. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email “Helen Haines is a deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community.” ‘Completely shocking’ Guardian Australia has spoken to local residents who have been concerned about Nugent’s behaviour for several years, including multiple allegations of abuse and threats from him. They reported erratic behaviour, shouting and music playing loudly until the early hours of the morning. They also raised concerns about his mental health. Nugent is a long-term forestry campaigner in the state’s north-east. Environment campaigners who worked with Nugent several years ago have expressed shock at his arrest. Nugent has a master’s of forest ecosystems science from the University of Melbourne and spent years researching the forestry industry in Victoria. He has also been a registered business owner in Wangaratta. Nugent was a committee member for the Save our Strathbogie Forest group, which campaigns against logging in the region. He became inactive around 2019-20. His arrest has shocked the group’s chair, Bertrant Lobert, who said he initially appeared to be “a reasonable and thoughtful person but then he drifted away”. “He was engaging, he was thoughtful and to hear what has happened now, if it all turns out to be true, is just completely shocking,” Lobert said. “This is quite personal as a lot of people in our group knew Helen personally and were friends. “This is more than just a tragedy about the targeting of public figures, it’s about our community and the people we know.” View image in fullscreen The scene of the alleged attack in Wangaratta. Photograph: Australian Broadcasting Corporation/Reuters Helen McKernan, the president of the Strathbogie Ranges Conservation Management Network Inc, also worked with Nugent as an activist before 2020. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion She says Nugent lost contact with her network of forestry campaigners around this date. “He was a committed activist,” McKernan said. “He would sleep out if necessary and help behind the scenes. We could always rely on him to turn up and contribute.” “It’s just a shock.” When the then-Victorian minister for environment, Lily D’Ambrosio, visited the Strathbogie forest in November 2019 to announce a ban on native forest logging, Nugent was among a group of about a dozen environmentalists who posed for photos. Also among the group was Rebecca Swift, a friend of Dezi Freeman who owned the property where he was living when two police officers were killed and a third injured in a shooting last year. Swift and Freeman shared conspiratorial beliefs about government and the Covid-19 pandemic, but it is unclear whether Nugent also embraced those views. “Lily I was so pleased to be in the Strathbogie forest to hear your announcement today,” Swift commented on D’Ambrosio’s Facebook post announcing the logging ban. “You gave us heart and hope that we are heard, and that our beloved wild landscapes are valued for so much more than merely dollars. Forest and wildlife defenders welcome a future where we can assist genuine governments to care for our national parks.” Swift was contacted for comment. The Victorian Nationals MP Tim McCurdy said Nugent was known to his Wangaratta office and regularly came in to raise different issues. “He’s been at our office,” McCurdy said. “We get plenty of people come in, half a dozen a day come for various things. So yes, he’s been into our office, [to raise] various issues. “Our office didn’t feel threatened by him, if they had they would ring the police. I want to wish Helen all the best.” In October 2019, when Nugent was still actively campaigning on forestry issues, he praised Haines for her stance on climate change. When Haines posted on X about an ABC Q+A episode, Nugent wrote “Would’ve been nice to include a politician who takes climate change seriously, such as yourself”. – with AAP Explore more on these topics Helen Haines Australian politics Victoria news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Brendan Nugent facing three charges over alleged attack on MP Helen Haines Helen Haines loses leg as surgeons fight to save the other after alleged attack in Wangaratta A chaotic few minutes and a beloved MP’s life in the balance: a community grapples with the unfathomable Helen Haines is in a critical condition after an alleged attack. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text: An overnight Russian drone attack hit a hospital in Kyiv. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian View image in fullscreen An overnight Russian drone attack hit a hospital in Kyiv. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian Ukraine Russia strikes hospital in central Kyiv after SpaceX system falters again Volodymyr Zelenskyy says speed restrictions on Starshield system made it harder for Ukraine to shoot down drones Europe live – latest updates Luke Harding in Kyiv Fri 13 Nov 2026 06.24 EST Last modified on Fri 13 Nov 2026 08.26 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Russia has attacked a hospital in the centre of Kyiv, close to several western embassies, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield system had made it harder for Ukraine to shoot down enemy drones. Three people were injured when a drone smashed into the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics at 3am, hitting the second floor of the hospital and an adjoining 19th-century building. Meanwhile, Russia claimed it had shot down nearly 1,200 Ukrainian drones overnight, one of the largest swarms sent by Kyiv. It reported that at least four people were killed in the southern region of Volgograd. Russian drone strikes a medical facility in Kyiv The blast in Kyiv blew out windows in nearby buildings including in the National Academy of Arts across the road. The six-storey hospital is located in the Shevchenkivskyi district, not far from the Danish and Romanian embassies, as well as cafes and a park popular with dog walkers. Standing in the yard as smoke billowed from the burning building, and firefighters led dazed patients to safety, one witness, Oleksandr, said the attack had narrowly missed patients. “We were asleep when there was this massive boom. We all jumped out of bed straight away. “There was glass all over the floor. People were running about … If it had hit a little further to the left it would have been much worse. We felt the shock wave.” He added: “Targeting the wounded – that’s really low. Russia attacks everything. Where I live, high-rise blocks are being constantly hit by bombs. They don’t care where they drop them, or where they land.” View image in fullscreen Ukraine says the attacks are part of an illegal campaign of terror. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian Russia has recently stepped up its strikes on Ukraine’s civilian infrastructure, hitting power plants, passenger trains and two bridges across the Dnipro river. Ukraine says the attacks are part of a campaign of terror, designed to make a weary population capitulate. On Thursday, Zelenskyy said the Starshield system – operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX and overseen by the Pentagon – was again experiencing significant disruptions, after an unexplained slowdown last month. He said some Russian aerial sorties had got through because Ukrainian interceptor systems that rely on the US satellite service could not reach the necessary speed to knock out enemy drones. Starshield is the Ukrainian military’s version of Starlink. View image in fullscreen After the strike, firefighters led dazed patients to safety. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian The White House has yet to explain why the service has been throttled for a second time, but it comes after intense US-led shuttle diplomacy this week, with Donald Trump seemingly pressuring Zelenskyy to make territorial concessions to Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin. Trump’s emissaries, his son-in-law Jared Kushner and the real estate developer Steve Witkoff, met Putin in Moscow on Thursday. They then flew to Dublin to brief Zelenskyy on their talks, which came after trilateral negotiations on Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi. Kremlin negotiators insist that Ukraine hand over four Ukrainian provinces, including cities and villages Russian troops have been unable to conquer. They are also calling for a new “security architecture” in Europe – a demand in effect that Nato go back to its pre-1997 posture, before eastern European nations joined the alliance. View image in fullscreen Emergency services working at the hospital. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian At the same time, Moscow does not want European states to be involved in US-brokered talks to end the war in Ukraine. On Thursday, France’s president, Emmanuel Macron, said Europe had to take part since “US support” for Kyiv had ended. “Without Europeans, there is no support for Ukraine,” Macron said. “At the end of the day, we will be the ones to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.” Meanwhile, Russian strikes ⁠on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ⁠overnight caused ⁠power ​outages in 12 ⁠regions, said deputy energy minister Artem ⁠Nekrasov. The ‌affected regions are ‌Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Zhytomyr, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Kharkiv, ‌Khmelnytskyi and Chernihiv. “Energy workers ​are working at an intensified pace, ⁠but new attacks ​and constant ​air raid ​alerts ​are ‌complicating and delaying ​repairs,” ​Nekrasov said. In Kyiv, the orthopaedic hospital’s director, Roman Derkach, said medical services had been temporarily suspended as a cleanup operation got under way. Thirty patients were taken to safety. https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/19/iraq.text: Joint Iraqi forces will begin implementing a plan to redeploy security units in the Jurf al-Nasr area (formerly Jurf al-Sakhr) in the north of Babil province on Friday, the day of the government deadline given to Kataib Hezbollah to leave its stronghold before the armed forces enter it expires.That's according to an informed source, which spoke to the Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Thursday.According to the source, the redeployment will take place under security arrangements which divide responsibilities between army units, the federal police and the Popular Mobilisation Forces, as well as securing oil transport routes and reopening roads.The deployment plan, set out in a document issued by the director of the office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Lieutenant General Abdul Amir al-Shammari, defines the tasks of the security units in the area, based on official letters dated 15 and 16 November 2026.Details of the deployment planUnder the plan, the 38th Brigade of the Defence Ministry’s 10th Division will secure the area from the Ya Hussein berm to the Fadhiliya junction, extending to the boundary with Anbar Operations Command.The Federal Police’s 17th Brigade will take responsibility for central Jurf al-Nasr, covering the area between the Euphrates River to the east and the Musayyib-Fadhiliya road to the west.Two Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) units – the 72nd and 79th Brigades – will secure the area from the Musayyib-Fadhiliya road to the boundary with Karbala Operations Command.The plan also assigns an Energy Police regiment to protect oil transport routes. Babil police will set up a checkpoint at the Fadhiliya junction towards Musayyib, while Anbar police will establish another towards Ameriyat al-Fallujah.Authorities will also begin reopening the road linking Musayyib, Bahbahani, Fadhiliya junction and Ameriyat al-Fallujah.A counter-terrorism regiment stationed at al-Hamiya camp will remain on standby as a reserve force, under the direct authority of the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, to respond to any emergencies.On Wednesday, PMF chief Faleh al-Fayyad sent a proposal to the prime minister's office calling for PMF units to take responsibility for securing the area. The letter, seen by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), named the 72nd and 79th Brigades and the PMF Operations Command's Special Forces Regiment, with the Energy Police responsible for protecting the oil pipeline.Al-Fayyad's letter referred to an earlier directive from the commander-in-chief's office, numbered 1954 and dated 16 November 2026.The Iraqi government has since confirmed that a formal order has been issued to establish a command headquarters in Jurf, following instructions from the commander-in-chief. The headquarters will bring together one army brigade, one Federal Police brigade and two PMF brigades.It will oversee all security units in the designated area, with the aim of bringing the different forces under a single chain of command.Qaani holds talks as officials seek to contain crisisSeparately, Iraqi armed group Kataib Hezbollah said on Thursday that its secretary-general, Abu Hussein al-Hamidawi, had met Iran's Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani.The meeting was also attended by Badr Organisation chief Hadi al-Amiri and PMF leader Faleh al-Fayyad. In a statement reported by Agence France-Presse (AFP), the group said the discussions focused on the crisis, describing their outcome as "good". It did not disclose when or where the meeting took place.Two Iraqi political sources told AFP on Tuesday that Qaani had also met Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi in Baghdad on Monday to discuss tensions surrounding Jurf al-Sakhr.Qaani took over as head of the Quds Force after his predecessor, Qasem Soleimani, was killed in a US strike near Baghdad airport in January 2020. He has made several visits to Iraq since then, although his trips are rarely officially announced.Oil smuggling allegations fuel dispute over withdrawalTensions between Prime Minister al-Zaidi's government and Kataib Hezbollah have escalated after he ordered the armed forces to enter Jurf al-Sakhr (al-Nasr) and gave the armed group until Friday to withdraw.The deadline follows an investigation by a government committee which Baghdad says uncovered evidence of oil smuggling in the area.Government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi said authorities had drawn up a plan to clear the area of anyone exploiting Iraq's oil wealth, which belongs to the country's people under the constitution.Kataib Hezbollah has rejected the allegations, accusing the prime minister's office of fabricating the case to force the group to surrender its weapons.On Tuesday, the faction organised a media tour of Jurf al-Sakhr, attended by several outlets, including Agence France-Presse (AFP).During the visit, senior figure Abu Taleb al-Saidi insisted the group would not leave the area "even over our dead bodies", while also saying it did not want "bloodshed".US pressure mounts over armed factionsThe standoff comes as Washington steps up pressure on Baghdad to bring armed groups with close ties to Tehran under government control and disarm them.Al-Zaidi, who has led the government for more than six months with US backing, pledged to tackle the issue when he took office. While some factions have indicated they are willing to cooperate, Kataib Hezbollah has refused to give up its weapons.The final deadline for armed groups to hand over their weapons is 30 June 2027.Jurf al-Nasr, formerly known as Jurf al-Sakhr, lies around 100 kilometres south of Baghdad.Iraqi forces and Popular Mobilisation units retook the area from the Islamic State group in 2014. It has remained under tight security ever since, with Kataib Hezbollah among the most influential armed factions operating there.The return of many residents displaced during the fighting has also yet to take place.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/trum.text: Guvernul SUA face presiuni pentru un acord de pace rapid între Ucraina și Rusia până la începutul lunii ianuarie, înainte ca democrații să preia controlul asupra Congresului SUA în urma victoriei lor în alegerile de la jumătatea mandatului, scrie Financial Times , care citează patru persoane informate cu privire la discuții. Emisarul special al SUA, Steve Witkoff, și ginerele președintelui Trump, Jared Kushner, au intensificat recent presiunea asupra aliaților europeni și a Kievului în timpul discuțiilor de la Moscova, Dublin și Berlin. Trimisul special al lui Donald Trump, Steve Witkoff, și ginerele său, Jared Kushner, au reluat negocierile cu Ucraina și Rusia la Abu Dhabi la începutul acestei luni, punând capăt unei pauze de opt luni cauzate de războiul din Iran. Partidul Republican al lui Trump a pierdut controlul atât asupra Camerei Reprezentanților, cât și asupra Senatului în alegerile de la jumătatea mandatului de la începutul acestei luni - democrații urmând probabil să încerce să consolideze sprijinul acordat Ucrainei și să intensifice presiunea asupra Moscovei. Președintele SUA s-a întâlnit cu Vladimir Putin în China săptămâna aceasta, declarând ulterior că omologul său rus a precizat clar că Moscova este „pregătită pentru pace”. Kushner și Witkoff au avut, de asemenea, o serie de întâlniri cu oficiali ruși, ucraineni și europeni la Moscova, Dublin și Berlin în ultimele zile, unde au transmis acest sentiment de urgență, au afirmat surse familiarizate cu discuțiile. „Americanii exercită o presiune puternică și există o oarecare îngrijorare că ar fi nevoie de concesii semnificative din partea Ucrainei pentru a se ajunge măcar aproape de un acord”, a declarat un oficial european după întâlnirea cu Kushner și Witkoff. „Americanii se grăbesc, Putin nu se grăbește”, a spus un altul. Acest calendar a amplificat îngrijorările la Kiev că președintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski ar putea fi forțat să accepte un acord în condițiile impuse de Moscova înainte ca democrații să preia controlul asupra Congresului, a declarat un înalt oficial ucrainean. Acest lucru provine din îngrijorările de la Casa Albă că noul Congres, care va fi format în ianuarie, ar putea extinde sprijinul pentru Ucraina și ar putea restricționa spațiul de manevră al administrației Trump prin sancțiuni mai dure împotriva Moscovei și anchete parlamentare. La Kiev și în capitalele europene, această cronologie a stârnit îngrijorări cu privire la faptul că președintele Volodimir Zelenski este forțat să facă concesii ample, inclusiv concesii teritoriale în Donbas, renunțarea la statutul de membru NATO și limitarea dimensiunii forțelor armate ucrainene. Oficialii guvernului ucrainean interpretează, de asemenea, recentele întârzieri în livrarea rachetelor antiaeriene Patriot și restricțiile asupra sistemului de sateliți Starshield drept tactici deliberate de presiune din partea Washingtonului. „Lui Trump îi place Putin și vrea să încheie totul până în ianuarie”, a declarat înaltul oficial, subliniind că Rusia „ar putea obține condiții mai bune” dacă acordul s-ar încheia înainte de ianuarie. Deși Trump deține autoritate extinsă pentru a conduce negocierile de pace, democrații din Congres sunt dornici să-și folosească puterile legislative pentru a consolida sprijinul acordat Ucrainei și pentru a impune sancțiuni suplimentare împotriva Moscovei. De asemenea, aceștia s-au angajat să-și folosească competențele de control pentru a examina politica externă a lui Trump și interesele de afaceri ale lui Witkoff și Kushner. Deși SUA nu au presat Ucraina să facă concesii specifice față de Rusia, Putin a cerut joi, după summitul său cu Trump și cu președintele Chinei, Xi Jinping, de la Shenzhen, ca Ucraina și aliații săi europeni să accepte „compromisuri” și „realități”. Printre acestea se numără o cerere de lungă durată ca Kievul să cedeze teritoriu Moscovei în regiunea crucială de pe linia frontului din Donbas, precum și interzicerea viitoarei aderări a Ucrainei la NATO și impunerea de limite asupra forțelor sale armate. Rusia a insistat, de asemenea, pentru schimbări radicale ale ordinii de securitate europene de după Războiul Rece, în cadrul căreia NATO ar retrage trupele și armamentul de pe flancul său estic. Oficialii americani au sugerat, de asemenea, că Trump ar putea purta discuții cu liderii europeni despre modalitățile de a pune capăt războiului în cadrul summitului G20 pe care îl va găzdui la Miami luna viitoare, potrivit celor doi oficiali. Însă un înalt oficial francez a declarat că nu vor avea loc negocieri cu europenii pe tema Ucrainei la summitul G20, deoarece Ucraina nu a fost invitată. Trump l-a invitat pe Putin la summit, deși liderul rus nu a precizat dacă va participa. Oficialii ucraineni au interpretat recentele restricții de viteză impuse sistemului „Starshield” — versiunea militară a sistemului de comunicații prin satelit „Starlink” al lui Elon Musk, realizat de SpaceX — alături de întârzierile din ultimele luni în livrarea rachetelor interceptoare „Patriot”, ca parte a eforturilor SUA de a slăbi poziția Kievului și de a spori presiunea asupra acestuia pentru a face concesii Rusiei. Înaltul oficial ucrainean a descris acțiunile administrației Trump drept „o alegere clară” de a ajuta Rusia să obțină condiții favorabile în negocierile de pace. Rusia dorește să utilizeze campania de lovituri aeriene planificată pentru a-și spori pârghia de negociere asupra Ucrainei în discuțiile viitoare, ceea ce face improbabil ca Moscova să fie de acord cu un acord rapid, potrivit a două persoane informate cu privire la gândirea Kremlinului. Abia recent negocierile au început să abordeze cererile Rusiei privind chestiuni mai ample de securitate în Europa, despre care Putin a afirmat că trebuie să facă parte din orice acord final. Acest lucru face și mai puțin probabil ca Moscova să fie de acord cu acordul rapid pe care Trump îl promovează, cu excepția cazului în care Ucraina și aliații săi europeni cedează în fața cererilor lor. Țările europene, care doresc mai întâi un armistițiu înainte de a lua în considerare discuțiile privind cadrul mai larg de securitate al Europei, au solicitat un rol oficial în cadrul negocierilor, iar Rusia a afirmat că orice acord final ar necesita contribuția acestora. Putin nu s-a angajat însă încă să extindă negocierile și a declarat că Rusia va lua o decizie abia după ce oficialii europeni se vor întâlni cu omologii lor la Moscova. Oficialii americani încearcă să rezolve simultan disputele teritoriale și problemele mai ample legate de securitatea europeană, considerând că ambele sunt esențiale pentru încheierea războiului. SUA au mai afirmat că Moscova este de acord cu un eventual acord prin care Ucraina să primească garanții de securitate din partea țărilor occidentale, după modelul clauzei de apărare reciprocă prevăzută la articolul 5 al NATO. „Cred că președintele Trump este deschis la această idee, dar, evident, acest lucru trebuie să fie în interesul Americii”, a declarat Kushner joi, la Berlin. El a adăugat: „Cred că i-am convins pe ruși să accepte acest concept, conform căruia orice garanție de securitate pentru Ucraina s-ar baza pe articolul 5.” Însă Serghei Riabkov, viceministru rus al Afacerilor Externe care a participat la ultima rundă de negocieri de la Abu Dhabi, a declarat vineri că „chiar și o formulă de aderare quasi-NATO pentru Kiev . . . este o opțiune inacceptabilă pentru noi”, potrivit Interfax. „Să recunoască inviolabilitatea cererii noastre ca Ucraina să nu poată adera niciodată la NATO.
